paper.title: Meta-Learning Hypothesis Spaces for Sequential Decision-making

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian optimization / kernelized bandit with unknown kernel and offline meta-data
unmapped: The true kernel is unknown; it is a sparse nonnegative combination of p known finite-dimensional base kernels
Learner has offline meta-data from m related tasks with n samples each, all functions in the same RKHS with norm <= B
Kernel is meta-learned via group Lasso (Meta-KeL) before the bandit interaction
settings.definition_quote: Consider a sequential decision-making problem, where the agent repeatedly interacts with an environment and makes observations y_t = f(x_t) + \varepsilon_t of an unknown function f: X -> R residing in an RKHS H_{k^*} that corresponds to an unknown kernel function k^*. We further assume that the function has a bounded kernel norm ||f||_{k^*} <= B and that the domain X subset R^{d_0} is compact.

bound.expression_latex: \sqrt{\hat d T\log T}\Big( B\big(1 + \epsilon(n,m)\big) + \sqrt{\hat d \log T+ \log1/\delta}\Big)
bound.regime: n, m large enough that eps(n,m) <= c_1

symbols.d_hat: sum of feature dimensions d_j of base kernels active in the meta-learned kernel
symbols.eps_nm: meta-learning error epsilon(n,m) = 32 sigma s/(kappa^2 sqrt(mn)) * sqrt(1 + (2/m)(log(2p/delta) + sqrt(m d_max log(2p/delta))))

conditions: f in RKHS of unknown k^* with ||f||_{k^*} <= B (S = B)
k^* is a nonnegative combination of p known normalized finite-dimensional base kernels with ||eta*||_1 <= 1
Restricted eigenvalue condition on meta-data (Assumption 4.2) with kappa(s), |J_{k*}| <= s
zero-mean sub-Gaussian noise with variance proxy sigma^2
tuning: lambda >= 4 sigma/sqrt(mn) sqrt(1 + (2/m)(log(2p/delta) + sqrt(m d_max log(2p/delta))))
nu_t = B(1+eps(n,m)/2c_1) + sigma sqrt(d_hat log(1 + t/(c_1 bar_sigma^2)) + 2 + 2 log(1/delta))

source.label: cor:regret_bound
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$. Suppose $f\in \tH$ with $\norm{f}_\tk \leq B$ and that values of $f$ are observed with zero-mean sub-Gaussian noise of variance proxy $\sigma^2$. Then, with probability greater than $1-\delta$, \textsc{GP-UCB} used together with $\khat$ satisfies $R_T= \gO( \sqrt{\hat d T\log T} ( B(1 + \epsilon(n,m)) + \sqrt{\hat d \log T+ \log1/\delta}))$ provided that the exploration coefficient is set to ...

results.notes: Regret R_T = sum f(x*) - f(x_t), realized regret bounded w.h.p. Assumptions of Theorem 4.3 (meta-data conditions) are implicitly required. Horizon: nu_t does not depend on T, so treated as anytime. Theorems 4.3, 5.1 (kernel recovery / confidence bounds) and Prop 4.4 (sparsity) are not regret guarantees and were not recorded.

cited_results.setting_description: Kernelized bandit with known kernel, f in RKHS with norm <= B, sub-Gaussian noise; high-probability regret
